property_summary: After any call to transferOwnership, the owner should remain unchanged unless the caller is the current owner. The bug allows any caller to change the owner.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner must remain unchanged; the bug allows any caller to change it.
The owner remains unchanged after a non-owner calls transferOwnership in the reference contract, but changes in the buggy version.
For any caller, after calling transferOwnership the resulting owner is the input newOwner, which holds for the reference when the caller is owner, but the buggy version makes it true for any caller.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner must either be the old owner or the newOwner parameter; the buggy version can set owner to newOwner even when called by a non-owner.

For any two distinct addresses (attacker, newOwner) where attacker is not the current owner, after attacker calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner must remain unchanged in the reference, but the buggy version sets owner to newOwner.

For any caller, if ownership has been transferred to that caller, the owner remains that caller until a subsequent (authorised) transfer; the bug allows any caller to change ownership to themselves without authorisation.
For any caller who is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership must leave the owner unchanged; the bug allows any caller to succeed and change owner to any address arbitrarily.
For any caller who is not the current owner, a transferOwnership call must revert and leave the owner unchanged; the bug removes the revert, allowing any caller to change the owner to any address.
Rule: For any caller that is not the owner, the `owned()` function must revert. The bug removes the `onlyOwner` modifier, so a non-owner can call `owned()` without revert.
Only the owner can call owned() without reverting; the buggy modifier inverts the check so non-owner calls succeed and owner calls revert.
Only the owner can successfully call owned(). In the reference, a non-owner call reverts; in the mutant, any caller succeeds.
The owned() function should succeed when called by the owner; the buggy modifier always reverts, so owned() fails even for the owner.
For any address, calling owned() reverts iff the caller is not the current owner; the bug makes it revert for all callers including the owner.
In the reference contract, calling owned() never reverts when the caller is the current owner; the buggy contract always reverts on owned() regardless of caller.
In the reference contract, calling owned() by the current owner never reverts; the buggy modifier always reverts, so owned() reverts even for the owner.
For any non-zero address appointed as owner, transferring ownership to that address and then calling owned() as the new owner succeeds in the reference but reverts in the buggy version.
